# Sakura

> A complete coding agent you can build with. Sakura is a TypeScript library: create a working coding agent in a few lines, then define only what makes your agent different (tools, environment, goal, review, sub-agents) instead of rebuilding the loop, tool protocol, context, sessions and recovery.

Names:
- Sakura: the framework.
- sakura-agent: the npm package. Install with `npm install sakura-agent`. Needs Node 22.18 or newer.
- sakuracode (Sakura Code): a terminal coding agent built on Sakura. Install: `npm install -g sakuracode`.
- Infinity: an evaluation-driven system that runs many agents in parallel, built on Sakura.

Links:
- GitHub: https://github.com/Vist233/Sakura
- npm (library): https://www.npmjs.com/package/sakura-agent
- npm (terminal): https://www.npmjs.com/package/sakuracode
- Site (English): https://sakura.zhangyvjing.com/
- Site (Chinese): https://sakura.zhangyvjing.com/zh/
- Licence: MIT

Design:
- Three interfaces: `LlmClient` (talking to models), `Log` (what happened and how to resume), `Environment` (where tools run: local, SSH, Docker).
- Five layers: Data; Core (kernel, llm, env, session, testing); Plugins (context, tools, resilience, limits, review, redaction, agents, toolset, trace); Assembly (createAgent, corePlugins, compose); Products. Boundaries are checked on every build; plugins never import each other.
- Sub-agents inherit the parent's plugins except agents, limits, context and tools by default, so review and redaction carry over; change it with `subAgents.notInherited`.
- The host application decides how many agents run, the model budget and heavy-work concurrency.

Safety:
Sakura ships no sandbox. SSH and Docker are places to run, not sandboxes. `confine` bounds the file tools, not the shell. Run untrusted work in isolation you provide.

Evidence (real runs, each with its conditions; not one experiment):
- Real usage: 168 Sakura Code sessions on one machine, 2026-11-09 to 11-18, 9 active days; 7,150 tool calls; 101 compactions after which the work went on; 98.6 % prompt cache hit (the cache is the provider's).
- Execution review (records from 2026-11-10 18:34): 5,314 decisions, 75 denials; 42 of them real risks after checking each one (deletions, credentials, privilege, download-and-run); 18 cancelled runs, 13 rule false positives, 2 human or cache.
- Sakura Code on Terminal-Bench 2.1: 75/88, one local run, Pass@1 85.23 %. Not a leaderboard score.
- Unattended: 20.8 hours, 1,822 model requests, 1,796 tool calls; the session ran 43.7 hours in all.
- Infinity, 16 vCPU, 16 agents sharing 8 heavy-work slots: time to the first scored result 29.3 to 16.5 minutes.
